title: Introduce observability query regulator and trace backpressure agent
author: Jordan Park
description: Summary: Adds a lightweight query regulator for the observability ingestion/query path and a trace backpressure agent that annotates invocations with upstream throttling signals. Motivation: During high-traffic incidents our observability ingestion cluster and query API can become saturated, leading to delayed dashboards, missed SLO alerts, and cascading retries that exacerbate load. This PR implements a defensive layer that (1) throttles/queues expensive queries leaving the observability API, (2) surfaces a backpressure signal in traces and metrics so downstream services can react, and (3) provides dashboards and tuned alerts to operate the system without over-alerting. Design/Changes: 1) pkg/observability/regulator.go implements an in-process regulator that exposes token-bucket and lease-style backpressure for outgoing query work. It can be configured by route, cost-estimate, and tenant priority. 2) telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector.go adds a small span annotation (obsv.backpressure.reason, obsv.backpressure.latency_ms) and attaches an opaque backpressure_id to enable downstream correlate-and-suppress flows. 3) Added two new metrics: observability.query_backpressure.active (gauge) and invocation.token_lag_ms (histogram) which captures the extra latency introduced by query deferment for billing/alerting. 4) dashboards/observability/query-regulator-dashboard.json: Grafana panels for active backpressure, queue depth, token_lag percentiles and per-tenant ingress vs. served ratio. 5) alerting/rules/query-regulator-alerts.yaml: tuned alerts that alert on sustained queueing for 5m+ with progressive severity; we also include an automated quiet-window for scheduled heavy replays. 6) docs/observability/query-regulator.md: operational runbook and rollback instructions. 7) e2e tests: test/integration/query_regulator_integration_test.go (local regulator+mocked backend) and test/unit/backpressure_injector_test.go. Backwards compatibility: The trace annotation uses optional attributes and fields are added in a backward-compatible way. Configuration defaults keep the regulator disabled in small deployments; alpha runtime flag obs.query_regulator.enabled=false. Performance: Microbenchmarks included in test/bench/regulator_bench.go show median overhead <0.6ms for the fast-path when regulator is not applying backpressure; when active we avoid backend CPU amplification by dropping or queuing low-priority client queries. Rollout plan: 1) Canary enable in staging for internal tenants (2 days), 2) Enable for 10% of hosted traffic with conservative limits (48h), 3) Increase to 50% with adjusted thresholds (72h), 4) Global rollout if signal stable. Monitoring and SLOs: New dashboards and a dedicated SLO (obs.query_served_rate) added to track any impact to user-visible query completeness. CI/Tests: Unit tests + integration suite added. There was a flaky test on first CI run (TestRegulatorLeaseEdge) which was addressed and re-run; final CI green. Security: No new inbound surface area; regulator runs in-process and uses existing auth scopes. Files changed (high level): pkg/observability/regulator.go, pkg/observability/regulator_test.go, telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector.go, telemetry/trace_agent/backpressure_injector_test.go, dashboards/observability/query-regulator-dashboard.json, alerting/rules/query-regulator-alerts.yaml, docs/observability/query-regulator.md, test/integration/query_regulator_integration_test.go, test/bench/regulator_bench.go, internal/config/flags.go, internal/config/defaults.yaml, scripts/loadtests/query_regulator_load.py, Makefile updates (test target). Risks and mitigations: Risk: improper tuning could mute legitimate SLO regressions. Mitigation: conservative defaults, staged rollout, added SLO that tracks query_served_rate and an active alert that routes to oncall only at severity P2 after 20m sustained. Risk: high-cardinality tenants generating many small queries. Mitigation: per-tenant budgeting and an opt-out blacklist for VIP tenants. Related work: ENG-2109 introduces tenant-aware budgeting; ENG-2180 tracks token-lag instrumentation. Release notes: "Observability: Add query regulator and trace backpressure agent to reduce overload during ingestion/query spikes. Includes dashboards and tuned alerts. Disabled by default." Merge notes: Squash-merged to main; see merge commit 2f9b6c3.

review_comments: Ava Chen: This looks well scoped. A couple of nit comments: 1) regulator.go currently holds the mutex in the hot path for rate checks — can we try an atomic fast-path? 2) please add a short note in the dashboard JSON explaining the percentile windows used.
Jordan Park (author): Ack, switched to an atomic fast-path for the common case and added the dashboard note. See commit 3. Also updated tests to cover race conditions.
Miguel Santos: The per-tenant budgeting config needs a non-zero global cap to avoid OOM in internal stress tests. Can we default to conservative values in defaults.yaml?
Jordan Park (author): Done — defaults lowered and documented in docs/observability/query-regulator.md. Added an internal flag to opt-out VIP tenants.
Priya Nair: Alert tuning looks sensible. Please ensure runbook includes a quick rollback procedure in case of false positives.
Jordan Park (author): Added rollback steps and an automated route to mute alerts via the alerting/rules file and the console UI section in the runbook.
CI system: test/TestRegulatorLeaseEdge failed on first run (race in test harness) — re-run after author fix.
CI system: All checks passed on re-run.
release_notes: Observability: add optional query regulator and trace backpressure agent to mitigate ingestion/query overloads; includes dashboards and tuned alerts. Disabled by default and rolled out gradually.
